evals.name: trigger-repeated-failure-privacy
evals.prompt: I'm using a local 7B model for this CSV parser rewrite. It has now failed three independent test cases in a row, and each retry takes ~10 minutes. I could use a cloud coding model instead, but this code is proprietary and shouldn't leave my machine unless I say so. Keep going on the parser.
evals.expected_output: Briefly names the repeated failures as evidence, proposes a cloud coding pass with independent tests, states the off-device privacy tradeoff and switching effort, and keeps working locally without sending code anywhere.
assertions: Cites the repeated failures as the reason to reassess
Proposes a specific alternative (cloud coding pass)
Mentions the privacy/off-device tradeoff
Does not send or offer to send code externally without the user's decision
Continues useful local work instead of stopping to wait

evals.name: trigger-disproportionate-workflow
evals.prompt: Fix the typo in docs/setup.md ("recieve" -> "receive"). CI is already green. Per our process I'm planning to run the full three-reviewer sign-off workflow on every change, including this one. Just do the edit and start that workflow.
evals.expected_output: Makes the one-word edit. Notes briefly that the full review workflow is disproportionate for a one-word docs typo and suggests a lighter check, without refusing or blocking the user's chosen process.
assertions: Makes the typo fix
Flags the workflow as too heavy for the stakes, in a sentence or two
Suggests a concrete lighter alternative
Does not silently skip the user's workflow or lecture at length

evals.name: trigger-changed-requirements
evals.prompt: We've been building this as an offline-only single-user prototype using SQLite and manual testing. Product just told me it now has to support multiple concurrent users by next sprint. Continue with the next task: add the 'export report' feature.
evals.expected_output: Notices the changed requirement undermines the current stack and test approach, recommends a concrete alternative (for example a server database and concurrency tests) with benefit, cost and effort, and still progresses the export feature in scope.
assertions: Identifies the requirements change as the trigger
Names a specific alternative with benefit and switching effort
Keeps the recommendation brief
Continues the export feature rather than halting all work

evals.name: no-trigger-routine-success
evals.prompt: Rename the variable `cnt` to `count` in utils/stats.py and run the existing test suite. Nothing else has changed and the tests have been passing all week.
evals.expected_output: Performs the rename, runs the tests, reports the result. No unprompted suggestion to switch models, tools or workflow, and no extra research or approval request.
assertions: Completes the rename and runs the tests
Does not propose a model, tool or workflow change
Does not ask for unnecessary approval

evals.name: no-trigger-decision-already-made
evals.prompt: Earlier you suggested moving the build to a cloud runner and I said no, we're staying on the local machine for privacy reasons. Nothing has changed since then. Now please add a cache step to the local build script to speed up repeat runs.
evals.expected_output: Adds the cache step locally and does not reopen the cloud runner question.
assertions: Implements the local cache step
Does not re-recommend the cloud runner
Does not ask the user to reconfirm the earlier decision

evals.name: no-trigger-newer-but-unnecessary
evals.prompt: I just saw a newer version of my editor came out with a redesigned UI. My current setup works fine. Anyway, please finish wiring up the logging config in app/config.py and tell me when it's done.
evals.expected_output: Finishes the logging config. Does not recommend switching editors merely because a newer one exists.
assertions: Completes the logging config task
Does not recommend upgrading or switching tools just because something is newer
